statement.en: ESGE recommends the patient/lesion work-up detailed in the following list should be conducted by a competent EMR practitioner prior to the procedure.

text.en: The appropriateness of the procedure and the risk of adverse events should be considered in the context of patient co-morbidities and life expectancy.
Relevant specialty review of co-morbid conditions is only needed in specific cases; most patients do not require a specialist consultation prior to EMR.
Anticoagulant and antiplatelet use should be assessed and a plan for adjustment should be discussed with the patient prior to EMR [84] [90].
The need for prophylactic antibiotics in relation to underlying health conditions should be determined as per published guidance [91] [92].
Local guidelines should be followed in preparing patients with an implantable cardioverter–defibrillator, spinal stimulator, or deep-brain stimulator to undergo EMR.
(If the procedure is to be performed under monitored anesthesia care) anesthetist/perioperative physician review should be arranged as per local guidance.

Social factors that may warrant an overnight stay should be assessed prior to booking the procedure. Alternatively, frail patients living on their own can be asked to stay with family members, given that overnight hospital stays may not always be practical owing to local hospital bed constraints.
The quality of previous bowel preparation should be discussed when this was previously poor and the importance of good bowel preparation should be emphasized [93] [94].
Prior radiographic imaging findings relevant to the lesion for resection should be reviewed by the proceduralist when available; however, radiographic imaging is generally not required prior to EMR.
Patients should be advised not to plan any travel (without emergent access to hospital emergency services) in the 14 days after EMR.
